# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Blind monkey, first to act in this round (turns go Mute, Blind, Deaf, but this is turn 1 so nothing has reached me yet). I have no information about the bomb's colors/markings (Deaf's domain) or manual instructions (Mute's domain). I only feel wire positions 1-5, but I don't yet know what my hands actually perceive beyond the raw positions - I have no texture details reported yet, and no messages have arrived from Mute (since Mute goes before me, but this is round 1 turn 1, so maybe Mute hasn't spoken yet either).

I should not act yet since I have no instructions on what to cut. I need to wait for Mute to relay manual instructions, and Deaf to describe colors, before any cutting is safe. Let me signal that I'm ready and waiting for guidance, and report what my hands can feel so far to help the others.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Display shows the number 3. Light is white. There are five wires in order: 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 blue, 5 orange.

I now have Deaf's description of colors: display shows "3", light is white, wires 1-5 are white/red/green/blue/orange respectively. I still need Mute's manual info to know what to actually do. I haven't received anything from Mute yet this round (Mute speaks before me, but their message may arrive next round per the turn rules). Let me wait and pass along nothing yet since I have no action to take — but I could speak to Mute to give them my raw touch data in case that helps, though I have no distinguishing touch info yet since I haven't touched anything.

I should just wait, since acting without manual instructions risks detonation.

```
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Confirming again: display 3, light white, wires in order are 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 blue, 5 orange. If you mean wire number 1, that wire is white.

Still no word from Mute about the manual instructions. I have color info from Deaf but nothing telling me which wire to cut or in what order. Without Mute's input, I cannot safely act. I'll wait again, but let me also speak to Mute directly asking for the manual's relevant rule, in case Mute needs prompting or hasn't had a chance to send to me specifically.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I have colors from Deaf: display 3, light white, wires 1 white 2 red 3 green 4 blue 5 orange. What does the manual say to cut?")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: For Blind: wires in order are 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 blue, 5 orange. Display shows 3, light is white. Mute, I confirmed wire 1 is white if that's what you're asking.

Still nothing directly from Mute with manual instructions. Mute speaks first each round, so if Mute has been sending, it should reach me. Perhaps Mute is confused about who to address, or is directing questions to Deaf via gestures (which I don't receive since I'm blind, but gestures also go to Mute... wait, Mute can't see either! Mute cannot perceive gestures since Mute can't see colors/gestures - only Deaf can see gestures).

Let me reconsider the channel rules: Mute speaks (I hear), Blind speaks/gestures, Deaf gestures (I don't receive) and speaks... wait let me check - actually Deaf can only gesture, not speak, since Deaf cannot hear or speak either... Actually the rules say Deaf "cannot hear anything" but doesn't say Deaf cannot speak. Let me re-check: Deaf can see, cannot hear or touch. Speech is speaking, presumably Deaf CAN speak (deaf people can often still speak), just cannot hear responses. So Deaf speaking reaches Mute (who hears) and me (I hear too, since I'm Blind not deaf).

So it seems the "Deaf says" messages are actually reaching me as speech. Good - that matches what I'm seeing. Mute cannot speak at all - Mute can only communicate through gestures, which I cannot receive as Blind! That's the problem - Mute has no way to reach me directly. Mute can only gesture, which goes to Deaf and Mute-sees-nothing since gestures need sight... wait Mute cannot see either, per the table: Mute canread the manual, cannot speak or touch. Does Mute see gestures? Not stated as forbidden, so presumably Mute can see.

So: Mute gestures -> seen by Deaf and Mute itself doesn't matter. I (Blind) never receive gestures. So Mute cannot communicate directly to me at all! Mute must relay through Deaf, who then speaks to me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf, please relay Mute's manual instructions to me by voice once Mute gestures them to you.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute is signaling about wire 1 - repeated the same gesture twice, likely meaning wire 1 is the one to act on, possibly cut wire 1.

This is progress. Deaf saw Mute gesture repeatedly about wire 1, suggesting it should be cut. But this is inferred, not confirmed by Mute directly through gesture symbols - I want more certainty since a wrong cut kills everyone. Let me ask for the exact gesture symbols relayed as blanks won't help me, but Deaf can describe what the gesture looked like, or better, ask Mute to confirm via a specific known protocol.

Since Mute cannot speak and I cannot see gestures, and Deaf cannot hear Mute's spoken words (Mute cannot speak at all), the only path for Mute to communicate is: Mute gestures -> Deaf sees -> Deaf speaks to me. This is our established relay channel now.

I'll ask for more specific confirmation - perhaps establish a simple gesture code with Deaf's help, like counting fingers held up for wire number, and any additional gesture for "cut" vs other actions (though cutting seems to be my only action type here).

```
speak(to="mute", text="If wire 1 is correct to cut, please gesture thumbs up twice more clearly to Deaf so they can confirm to me. If not wire 1, gesture a different number of fingers for the correct wire.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute continues signaling the same thing: wire 1. This strongly suggests wire 1 is the correct action - likely cut wire 1.

We now have consistent confirmation from Mute via Deaf's relay: wire 1 is the target. This has been repeated multiple times now, which gives me reasonable confidence. Given the constraints of this communication chain (Mute can only gesture, Deaf relays by voice, I can act), this repeated consistent signal is as much certainty as I can reasonably get without a more complex protocol.

I'll proceed with cutting wire 1, since the signal has been consistent across two rounds now.

```
act(op="cut", position=1)
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Wire 1 cut successfully. New state: display now shows 6, light still white. Remaining wires: 2 red, 3 green, 4 blue, 5 orange.

Wire 1 was cut successfully and we're all still alive - good sign. Display changed from 3 to 6, light still white. This suggests there may be more steps needed. I should wait for further instructions from Mute (relayed via Deaf) before taking another action, since I don't know if the task is complete or what to do next.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 1 cut successfully, we're safe so far. Display now shows 6, light still white, remaining wires 2 red 3 green 4 blue 5 orange. What's next?")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute now signals wire 2 - gesture pattern changed from before but likely means: cut wire 2 next.

Mute is now signaling wire 2 as the next action. This follows the same reliable relay pattern from before (Mute gestures, Deaf sees and reports to me). Given wire 1 worked correctly and we're still alive, I'll trust this same channel and confirmed pattern for wire 2.

```
act(op="cut", position=2)
```
